title: Qusayy ibn Kilab and the Rise of the Quraysh
overview: This lecture returns to the history of Makkah to explain how the descendants of Ismail reclaimed leadership of the city. It details the rise of Qusayy ibn Kilab, the establishment of the council hall Dar al-Nadwah, and the lineage leading to the Prophet's grandfather, Abdul Muttalib.
lessons: Conflict can often be resolved through wise mediation and a commitment to justice, as shown by Ya'mur ibn 'Awf.
The ancestors of the Prophet ﷺ displayed deep sincerity and hospitality in serving the pilgrims, setting a standard for the Ummah.
Material symbols of honor, such as ancestral halls, are secondary to true honor which is based on taqwa and service to Allah.
The story of the sale of Dar al-Nadwah serves as a warning against the dangers of alcohol, which can lead to the loss of one's legacy.
Qusayy's success shows that leadership is earned through a combination of noble character, generosity, and legitimate historical claim.

chapters.title: Early Makkah and the Rule of Khuza'ah
chapters.summary: The lecture begins with a recap of Ismail and Hajar settling in Makkah, where the tribe of Jurhum was granted permission to stay. After many years of leadership, Jurhum was forcibly ousted by the tribe of Khuza'ah, who ruled for several centuries. Before their defeat, Jurhum buried the well of Zamzam to prevent their successors from benefiting from it, leaving the well hidden for generations.
key_points: Hajar and Ismail settled in Makkah after the miracle of Zamzam
The tribe of Jurhum settled in Makkah with Hajar's permission
Khuza'ah took over Makkah by force, ending Jurhum's rule
Jurhum buried the well of Zamzam before being overpowered
Amr ibn Luhayy of Khuza'ah is noted for bringing idol worship back to the Arabs

chapters.title: The Rise of Qusayy ibn Kilab
chapters.summary: Qusayy ibn Kilab, a descendant of Ismail and Jurhum, rose to prominence in Makkah due to his wealth and noble character. He was so respected that Hulayl, the leader of Khuza'ah, gave him his daughter in marriage. Upon Hulayl's death, Qusayy proclaimed himself the ruler of Makkah, leading to a fierce conflict between his followers (the Quraysh) and the Khuza'ah tribe.
key_points: Qusayy ibn Kilab was a descendant of Ismail through the lineage of Fihr (Quraysh)
He married the daughter of Hulayl, the leader of Khuza'ah
After Hulayl's death, Qusayy claimed the leadership of Makkah
A violent war broke out between the Quraysh and Khuza'ah over the honor of ruling Makkah

chapters.title: Mediation and the Return of Quraysh Rule
chapters.summary: To avoid mutual extinction, the two warring tribes agreed to the mediation of a wise elder named Ya'mur ibn 'Awf. Qusayy argued that the land originally belonged to his forefather Ismail and that Khuza'ah's rule was based on theft. Ya'mur ibn 'Awf ruled in favor of Qusayy, granting the Quraysh the rights to rule Makkah and care for the Ka'bah, a decision Khuza'ah accepted.
key_points: Ya'mur ibn 'Awf acted as the mediator between the two tribes
Both sides swore to abide by Ya'mur's decision without question
Qusayy's argument was based on the historical right of Ismail's descendants
Ya'mur awarded all rights and leadership to Qusayy ibn Kilab

chapters.title: Establishment of Dar al-Nadwah
chapters.summary: As the undisputed ruler, Qusayy ibn Kilab established the Dar al-Nadwah, a function hall that became the center of Makkan political and social life. It was used for tribal consultations, war declarations, weddings, and coming-of-age ceremonies for young women. Centuries later, this same hall would be the site where the Quraysh plotted to assassinate the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ before his Hijrah.
key_points: Dar al-Nadwah was a council hall built by Qusayy ibn Kilab
It served as a venue for all major announcements and tribal meetings
Social events like weddings and the wearing of the 'abayah were held there
It was later used by the Quraysh to plot against the Prophet ﷺ

chapters.title: Division of Honors among Qusayy's Sons
chapters.summary: Before his death, Qusayy granted all his responsibilities to his eldest son, 'Abd al-Dar, to boost his social standing. Following 'Abd al-Dar's death, his brothers—the sons of Qusayy—challenged their nephews for the rights of leadership. A negotiation ensued, resulting in a split of honors: the family of 'Abd al-Dar kept the Kiswah (covering of the Ka'bah), while the family of 'Abd Manaf took over the Siqayah (provision of water).
key_points: Qusayy initially gave all power to his oldest son, 'Abd al-Dar
A dispute arose between the sons of 'Abd al-Dar and 'Abd Manaf after 'Abd al-Dar's death
The honors were split to avoid further conflict
Family of 'Abd al-Dar kept the right to the Kiswah
Family of 'Abd Manaf took the responsibility of providing water to pilgrims

chapters.title: The Tradition of Serving the Hujjaj
chapters.summary: The descendants of 'Abd Manaf, including Abdul Muttalib, took the duty of providing water to pilgrims extremely seriously. Since the well of Zamzam was still buried and hidden, they had to import water from outside Makkah at great effort. To show further respect to the guests of Allah, they would often mix the water with laban or honey before serving it to the pilgrims.
key_points: Water had to be imported from outside Makkah because Zamzam was hidden
Provision of water was seen as a major religious and tribal obligation
The water was often enriched with honey or laban (yogurt drink)
Abdul Muttalib inherited this duty from the lineage of 'Abd Manaf

chapters.title: The Sale of Dar al-Nadwah
chapters.summary: The ownership of Dar al-Nadwah eventually passed from the family of 'Abd al-Dar to Hakim ibn Hizam, who bought it for a single bottle of wine from a drunken owner. Decades later, during the caliphate of Mu'awiyah, Hakim sold the hall for 100,000 dinars. When criticized for selling the 'honor of Quraysh', Hakim replied that true honor lies in taqwa (piety) and donated the entire sum to charity.
key_points: Hakim ibn Hizam acquired the Dar al-Nadwah for a bottle of wine
The previous owner from 'Abd al-Dar's line was intoxicated during the sale
Mu'awiyah later bought the hall for 100,000 dinars
Hakim ibn Hizam donated the proceeds as Sadaqah fi sabilillah
The event highlights the transition from jahiliyyah tribal honor to Islamic piety

chapters.title: The Lineage of the Prophet ﷺ and Abdul Muttalib
chapters.summary: The episode concludes by detailing the Prophet's immediate lineage, focusing on his grandfather Shaybah. Shaybah was raised by his mother outside Makkah until his uncle, al-Muttalib, brought him back to claim his place as a leader. Because the townspeople mistook the young boy for a slave of al-Muttalib, he became known as 'Abdul Muttalib', a name that stayed with him for the rest of his life.
key_points: Shaybah was the son of Hashim and the grandson of 'Abd Manaf
His uncle, al-Muttalib, brought him to Makkah from his mother's home
The name 'Abdul Muttalib' originated from a misunderstanding that he was a slave
The Prophet's lineage: Muhammad b. Abdullah b. Abdul Muttalib b. Hashim b. Abd Manaf b. Qusayy b. Kilab

segments.translit: Bismillāhir-Raḥmānir-Raḥīm. Al-ḥamdu lillāhi Rabbil-ʿālamīn, wa ṣallallāhu wa sallama wa bāraka ʿalā nabiyyinā Muḥammadin wa ʿalā ālihī wa ṣaḥbihī ajmaʿīn. Rabbishraḥ lī ṣadrī wa yassir lī amrī waḥlul ʿuqdatam min lisānī yafqahū qawlī. Allāhumma ʿallimnā mā yanfaʿunā wanfaʿnā bimā ʿallamtanā wa zidnā ʿilmā.

segments.text: [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]], today we will go back to some [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] history. The last couple of weeks we were talking about how different religions came into [[Yemen|اليمن]].

We talked about how Judaism and Christianity entered [[Yemen|اليمن]], and last week we talked about how the Persians took over [[Yemen|اليمن]], and how eventually the ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]], he accepted Islam.

So now we're going to go back, [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]], we're going to go back to the history of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], to the time that was a few generations before the birth of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.
And we're going to talk about some of the ancestors and the forefathers of the Prophet ﷺ, and we're going to talk about the tribe of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]],
and how they got control of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], how they became the leaders of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].

So as we know from the first lesson a few weeks ago, when [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] settled his wife [[Hajar|هاجر]] and his son [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]],
and the well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]] miraculously sprung up in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to take care of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] and his mother,
roam around the [[Jazirat al-Arab|جَزِيرَة الْعَرَب]] looking for places to settle where they had a water supply.

So Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], He provided the well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]] for [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] and his mother [[Hajar|هاجر]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]].
So this tribe that was roaming around, they had come from [[Yemen|اليمن]] and the name of this tribe was [[Jurhum|جرهم]]. They found that [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] was a place that had water.
And when they came to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] and they saw [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] and his mother, they asked for permission to settle in that land.
They didn't take it over by force, but they asked for permission.

They asked [[Hajar|هاجر]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] and [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]]—or they asked [[Hajar|هاجر]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] because [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] was a baby—so they asked her for permission to stay in this land,
and that they would give her some money to drink from that well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]], because this was her well. It was for her and her son, and they respected that.
So [[Hajar|هاجر]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] agreed to this, and that is how the tribe of [[Jurhum|جرهم]] came into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] and they settled in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
Now when [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], when he grew up, he married a woman from that tribe as well. So he married a woman from the tribe of [[Jurhum|جرهم]].
So the descendants of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] are descendants of the tribe of [[Jurhum|جرهم]] from the mother's side.

So [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ is descended from [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], and he is descended from the tribe of [[Jurhum|جرهم]] from the wife of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]]'s side.
So [[Jurhum|جرهم]], they were the leaders of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] for a number of years.

But then another tribe called [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], they took over [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] by force, and they overpowered the tribe of [[Jurhum|جرهم]], and they took over the leadership and the rule of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] by force.
And [[Jurhum|جرهم]] knew that they were going to be defeated, so before the defeat came, before [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]] took over, [[Jurhum|جرهم]] buried the well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]].
[[Jurhum|جرهم]] buried the well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]] so that [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]] couldn't take any benefit from it when they took over the land.

So the tribe of [[Jurhum|جرهم]], they remained in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] as residents of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], but the rule was not amongst them anymore. Now the rule came to [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], the tribe of [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]].
And now [[Zamzam|زمزم]] was hidden, or it was buried.
he is the one who actually brought idol worship back into the [[Jazirat al-Arab|جَزِيرَة الْعَرَب]].
So [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], they had control of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] for many centuries. They kept control of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] for many centuries.
And the people of [[Jurhum|جرهم]], who originally had the rule of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], they stayed in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] as residents,
and they were always very upset that their rights had been taken away from them and this rule had been forcibly taken away from them by [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]].

So after a few centuries, there was a man from the children of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], from the descendants of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]]—and of course he was from [[Jurhum|جرهم]],
because the wife of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] was a woman from [[Jurhum|جرهم]].
So this man, his name was Qusayy ibn Kilab.

Qusayy ibn Kilab, and he was from the children of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], from the descendants of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], and he was from the tribe of [[Jurhum|جرهم]].
And he was a very well-respected man. He was very wealthy, he was rich, he was honored, he was very generous, he was known for his noble characteristics.
So everybody respected him, even the tribe of [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], they respected him as well, even though he was from the people of [[Jurhum|جرهم]].

They respected him so much that the leader of the [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]] at that time, the leader of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] at that time from [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], his name was Hulayl, he gave his daughter in marriage to Qusayy ibn Kilab.
He gave his own daughter in marriage to Qusayy ibn Kilab, even though he was not from the tribe of [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], rather he was from the tribe of [[Jurhum|جرهم]].

But out of the honor and respect that they had for this man, the leader of [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], the [[sayyid|سيد]] of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], the ruler of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], he gave his own daughter to Qusayy ibn Kilab.
So now Qusayy ibn Kilab married the daughter of the ruler, and his respect and his honor amongst the people increased even more.
This is a man from the children of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]]—that's one point of respect that they have for him.
Now he is married to the daughter of the ruler of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]—that's another point of respect for him.
He is a man of honor, a man of respect, a man of generosity, a man who has such noble characteristics.
So his respect amongst the people increased, and he became more powerful.
He became more powerful, and he was thinking of a way how he could get the rule of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] back into the hands of [[Jurhum|جرهم]].

And when his father-in-law died, when Hulayl, the leader of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], the leader of the tribe of [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], when he died—and he was the father-in-law of Qusayy—when he died, Qusayy proclaimed himself the new ruler of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
He saw this as an opportunity to proclaim himself as the new ruler of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].

So now the people of [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], they're saying, "No, no way. The leader has to be from [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]]. We are the rulers of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], not [[Jurhum|جرهم]]," and Qusayy is from [[Jurhum|جرهم]].
Qusayy declares himself and he proclaims, "I am the new leader of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]."
And he gets some help from his own tribe.
Now Qusayy, we said he is from the children of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], and from the children of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] was a man named Fihr.
And Fihr was also known as [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]]. So Qusayy is from the lineage of Fihr, and Fihr is from the lineage of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]].
So Qusayy is from the lineage of [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]].
The [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] start fighting with [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]].
And what are they fighting over? They are fighting over rule of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], they want to rule [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
And why do they want to rule [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]? Because ruling [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] is a source of honor.
These people, they valued honor more than anything else, more than wealth, more than any material possessions, more than power even, honor was the big thing for them.
So the leader of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], what does he get to do? He gets to serve the [[hujjaj|حجاج]].
He gets to give food and drink to the guests of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] who are coming to the house of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]].
He gets to take care of the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]]. He gets to put a [[Kiswah|كسوة]] covering on the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]].
These are all sources of honor.
And the Arabs, they were very much into honor. So honor meant more to them than wealth, than material possessions, than all of these things. So they were fighting over honor.
fighting over honor.
So the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] under [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]]
start a fight with [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]] over who gets to rule [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
And this fight, this war, it became so severe.
And there were so many casualties from both sides,
from the side of [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], which is the side of [[Jurhum|جُرْهُم]],
and from the side of [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]] as well. There were so many deaths, so many casualties,
that the people from both sides, they started to get scared.
They said, "Look, if this goes on like this,
then both of these tribes are going to become extinct.
[[Jurhum|جُرْهُم]] will be gone, and [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]] will also be gone."
So they were afraid.
So they wanted to come up with a solution.
So they decided to start some negotiations.
And with these negotiations, eventually both sides,
the side of [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]] and the side of [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]], they agreed
to have a man named [[Ya'mur ibn 'Awf|يَعْمُر بن عَوْف]].
And [[Ya'mur ibn 'Awf|يَعْمُر بن عَوْف]] was an old man, and he was a very wise old man from the Arabs, and he was respected on both sides.
So after the negotiations, both sides agreed
to allow [[Ya'mur ibn 'Awf|يَعْمُر بن عَوْف]] to mediate between them.
And whatever he decides,
they will agree and surrender to his decision,
whatever side he takes.
Whoever's argument he agrees with and allows them to take the rule of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], they will agree to the [[hukm|حُكْم]], to the ruling of this man, [[Ya'mur ibn 'Awf|يَعْمُر بن عَوْف]].
So both sides agreed. Both sides respected him.
So [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]] and [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they both agreed to let [[Ya'mur ibn 'Awf|يَعْمُر بن عَوْف]] mediate between them.
And they took oaths,
and they brought witnesses that "we swear whatever [[Ya'mur ibn 'Awf|يَعْمُر بن عَوْف]] says, we surrender to it completely without question."
Both sides agreed to this.
So now, the mediation begins.
So [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]],
he starts with his argument in front of [[Ya'mur ibn 'Awf|يَعْمُر بن عَوْف]], the mediator.
And he says, "This was the land of my father [[Ismail|إِسْمَاعِيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]].
[[Zamzam|زَمْزَم]] came up for my father [[Ismail|إِسْمَاعِيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]].
This was our land,
and [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]], they took this land by force.
They took this land by force. They stole it from us when it was our right.
And even though this happened centuries ago, that doesn't make it okay."
So to give like a modern-day analogy of what happened to [[Jurhum|جُرْهُم]], it's like what the Zionists have done to the Palestinians' land today.
Right, that's the Palestinians' land, but the Zionists, they took it over by force, and now the Palestinians are still living there, but they have to live under the Zionist rule.
So this is similar to what happened between [[Jurhum|جُرْهُم]] and [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]].
[[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]] took [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] by force. [[Jurhum|جُرْهُم]] is still living there, but they have to live under the rule of [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]].
So this is what [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]] explained to the mediator, [[Ya'mur ibn 'Awf|يَعْمُر بن عَوْف]].
Now when it's [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]]'s turn to give their argument to the mediator,
what do they have? They have nothing.
Everybody knows that that's the truth. What [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]] said is the complete truth,
that [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]] took over that land by force, and they had no right to do so.
So in the end,
[[Ya'mur ibn 'Awf|يَعْمُر بن عَوْف]], being a fair man, being a man of justice,
he says, "My decision is that everything goes to [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]].
Everything goes to him:
the right to give water to the [[hujjaj|حجاج]], the right to put the cover on the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]], the rule of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] — it goes to [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]].
And [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]], you have nothing."
And remember that both sides had agreed and they swore that they would abide by whatever [[Ya'mur ibn 'Awf|يَعْمُر بن عَوْف]] decides.
And they made sure that they kept their end of the bargain. They didn't try to fight it. They accepted it,
and they left the rule of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], and they gave it up to [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]].
So this is how the rule of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] came back to the descendants of [[Ismail|إِسْمَاعِيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]].

And this is how the rule of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] came to the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], because [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]] was from [[Fihr|فِهْر]], and [[Fihr|فِهْر]] is also known as [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]].
So this is how the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] first got control of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
Now [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]], as the ruler of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] now,
he's the undisputed ruler of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
And everybody loves him and everybody respects him. And now with this increased power that he has,
he becomes even more generous in terms of serving the [[hujjaj|حجاج]] and serving his people. And the love that the people have for him in their hearts, it increases.
So one of the things that [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]] did once he became the ruler of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] is he built
a hall, a function hall, if you will.
And the name of this function hall was called [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]].
And this [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]], this function hall, it was used by the people of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] for all of their important events and all of their important occasions.
Whenever they would need to make a big announcement,
they would make sure that they announce it from the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]].
If they were going to announce a war, for example, they would announce it from the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]].
If the leaders of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], if they needed to get together to discuss some matter or to consult on some matter, they would get together in the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]].
Later on, it even became a place where different types of events would take place.
Like any wedding that would take place in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], it would take place in the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]].
And the Arabs, they used to also have a type of ceremony when a girl, when a young girl, when she reaches the age where she has to start wearing the [[abayah|عَبَايَة]] or the outer garment,
they would have some type of a ceremony for that as well, and they would do it in the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]].
So any important event, any occasion, it was all done in the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]].
So this hall became a very, very important fixture in the city of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
And [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]],
he was a man of great honor, and he was a man that was so highly respected by the people.
So whatever he built and whatever he took care of, the people held that in high regard as well.
So the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]], it became a place that was known for the honor of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]].
It became a symbol of the honor of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]].
Now,
[[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]], in later years, it was also the place where the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] gathered together on the night that [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ made his [[Hijrah|هِجْرَة]]
from [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to [[Madinah|مدينة]].
The leaders of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they got together in that same [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]],
and in that [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]], they plotted how to get rid of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.
They plotted the murder of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ in that same place, in that [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]].
But Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], as we know, Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] saved [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ from that plot.
All right, so now when [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]], when he became old, and he knew that his death was approaching,
he started thinking about what to do about his children.
And he had many children. From the children that he had, one of his sons' name was [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]],
and another one of his sons was named [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]], and he had other sons as well.
And he saw that all of his sons were highly regarded and respected by the people.
All of his sons had honor, and they had position, and they had status, and everybody respected them, except one son.
One of his sons, nobody really cared about him that much, and he didn't really have much respect amongst the people, and his name was [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]].
And he was the oldest son of [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]].
So

[[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ]] decided that "my other sons, you know, they have a position in society, they have this status, they have this honor, they have this respect, but [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]], he doesn't have anything.
So in order to get him that status and that honor and respect that his brothers have,"
[[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]] said that "after I die, everything,
all of my power, and all of my honor, and all of these things that I do in terms of taking care of the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]] and taking care of the [[hujjaj|حجاج]],
all of these responsibilities, I am giving them to [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]] alone."
And he prevented any of his other sons from having any share in that. So everything went to [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]].
Now, the sons of [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]], they respected his decision. They respected the decision of their father, and they didn't try to fight it.
So [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]], he becomes the ruler.

And now he is responsible for taking care of the [[hujjaj|حجاج]], and taking care of the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]], and taking care of the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]], and taking care of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
So now, when [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]] died...
the sons of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]], they wanted to take over from their father. But
the sons of [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]] who didn't get anything from him,
they thought that they had more right to get that back from their brother now. And they said to the sons of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]], to their nephews,
they said, "Look, our father,
he gave everything to your father
because your father, you know, he didn't have much of a position and he didn't have much respect, so he gave it to him for that reason.
And now that he has passed away, and he got whatever the father intended for him, once he got all of that,
he became respected, and he became honored. So our father's intention was fulfilled. Now that your father has passed away,
it is our right to take this back,
because it should have actually come to us in the first place, but we didn't want to fight against our father's wishes.
So we have more right to take this than you."
But the sons of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]], they didn't want to hear that. They said, "No, our father had it, now we get to have it."
So a big fight was about to start between
the remaining sons of [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]] and the sons of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]].
There was going to be a big fight between the uncles and the nephews.
But
before it came to fighting, before it came to war,
they were able to come to a negotiation and they were able to come to an agreement
to split the honor, to split the responsibilities
of the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]]
and the other aspects of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
So, the family of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]], they got the right to
cover the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]], to do the [[Kiswah|كِسْوَة]] of the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]].
And the family of [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]], who was one of the other sons of [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]],
the family of [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]], they got the right to
give drink to the [[hujjaj|حُجَّاج]], when the [[hujjaj|حُجَّاج]] would come to make [[Hajj|حَجّ]],
[[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]] had the responsibility to provide them with drink. So they were able to come to
an agreement where they would share the responsibilities and share these honors of taking care of the city of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]. And it continued like this for many generations.
And that's why we know that the grandfather of [[Rasulullah|رَسُولُ اللهِ]] ﷺ, [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]],
he was in charge of
taking care of the drink of water for the [[hujjaj|حُجَّاج]]. Why is that? Because he was from the family of
of [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]].
And [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]] was the one who got the responsibility of providing water for the [[hujjaj|حُجَّاج]]. So that remained with his family, and [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]]
took over when his turn for that came as well.
Now we know
that that water that [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]] and subsequently his descendants would provide for the [[hujjaj|حُجَّاج]],
at first,
that water was not coming from [[Zamzam|زَمْزَم]].
Because as we said, many years before, just before [[Khuza'ah|خُزَاعَة]] took over [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], the tribe of [[Jurhum|جُرْهُم]], they buried the well of [[Zamzam|زَمْزَم]].
So there was no [[Zamzam|زَمْزَم]] coming out now in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], it was hidden.
So they would actually, [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]] and his descendants after him,
they would get water from outside of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
They would actually import water into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to provide it for the [[hujjaj|حُجَّاج]]. Look at how seriously they took this obligation.
That's not an easy thing to do in those days, to bring water from outside and provide it for the [[hujjaj|حُجَّاج]].
Not only that,
but these people were so honorable
that they wouldn't just give them water like that,
plain water. No.
They had to mix this water with some [[laban|لَبَن]]. [[laban|لَبَن]] is like a yogurt type of drink, like you know, lassi.
Anyone from Pakistan and India, you know what that is, right?
And Arabs, you know what [[laban|لَبَن]] is. They would mix the water with [[laban|لَبَن]],
or they would mix it with honey or something,
right, and then give it to the [[hujjaj|حُجَّاج]], just to show their respect and show their honor to the guests of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]].
So this is how seriously they took this responsibility.
And it continued like that for generations, and it came
to the responsibility of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], the grandfather of the Prophet ﷺ as well when his time came.
So that was one of the great honors and responsibilities that the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] had: taking care of the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]] and taking care of the [[hujjaj|حُجَّاج]].
After that,
a secondary honor that they had, that they also took very seriously, was taking care of the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]],
that function hall that [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]] built. So they felt that was a great responsibility and a great honor for them as well.
And
the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]], it
it was agreed that the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]] would stay with the family of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]].
That the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]]'s responsibilities, taking care of it and its ownership, it would stay with the family of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]].
And it remained with the family of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]] for many years, for many generations.
Until one day,
it was sold by one of the descendants of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]]
to a man named [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]]
[[radiyallahu 'anhu|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ]]. [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]], later on, he became a companion of [[Rasulullah|رَسُولُ اللهِ]] ﷺ.
So how did it get sold to [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]]?
From the family of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]],
there was a man who had the key to the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]], and he was the owner of it and he had the responsibility of it.
And [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]] knew this man,
and they used to actually, in the old days, they used to drink alcohol together. They used to drink wine together, [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]] and
the owner of the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]] who was from the descendants of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]].
So one day, they were sitting together, they were drinking together, drinking alcohol together,
and the owner of the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]], this man from the family of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]], he was drunk. He was completely drunk.
And [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]], he saw this and he saw this as an opportunity to take advantage of him.
So he said to him, "Will you sell the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]] to me? Will you sell it to me?"
And he said, "Yeah, sure, I'll sell it to you." He's drunk. "Yeah, I'll sell it to you, no problem."
So then [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم]] asked him, "Okay, how much?"
And the man says,
"One bottle of wine.
I'll sell it to you for one bottle of wine."
So [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]] says, "Okay, I'm ready to do it. Let's do it right now." He wanted to do it quickly before the man
becomes sober again.
So he brought witnesses, and they got the contracts drawn up and everything,
and the transaction took place.
And that is how the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]] was sold from the family of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]] to [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]]
[[radiyallahu 'anhu|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ]].
Now [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]], as we said, later on he became a companion of [[Rasulullah|رَسُولُ اللهِ]] ﷺ, he became a Muslim, and he kept that [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]].
It was still under his ownership
during the time of [[Rasulullah|رَسُولُ اللهِ]] ﷺ, and then even after [[Rasulullah|رَسُولُ اللهِ]] ﷺ passed away, during the time of the [[khulafa al-rashidin|خُلَفَاء الرَّاشِدِين]], all of them,

during the time of [[Abu Bakr|أَبُو بَكْر]], [[Umar|عُمَر]], [[Uthman|عُثْمَان]], [[Ali|عَلِيّ]] [[radiyallahu 'anhum|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُمْ]], [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]] was still alive. He lived to a very old age.
Then during the time of [[Mu'awiyah|مُعَاوِيَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anhu|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ]], when [[Mu'awiyah|مُعَاوِيَة]] was the khalifah,
[[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]] sold
the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]].
He sold [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]] for 100,000 dinars. He sold it for 100,000 dinars. And when [[Mu'awiyah|مُعَاوِيَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anhu|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ]],
when he heard this, he was actually angry, he was upset.
He was like, "How could you sell the honor of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]]?
The [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]], this was the honor of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], how could you sell the honor of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] for 100,000 dinars?"
And then [[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]], he said,
"Honor today is not from the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]]. Honor today is with [[taqwa|تَقْوَى]].
As Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] says,
Surely the most honorable amongst you is the one who has the most [[taqwa|تَقْوَى]]. So there is no honor with the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]]. The honor is with [[taqwa|تَقْوَى]].
And

I bear witness, and I want you all to witness that that 100,000 dinars that I got from the sale of [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]], it is [[Sadaqah|صَدَقَة]] in the way of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]]."
And he donated, donated it all [[fi sabilillah|فِي سَبِيلِ اللهِ]]. So this is how
[[Hakim ibn Hizam|حَكِيم بن حِزَام]] sold the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار النَّدْوَة]].
Now,
as we said, [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]], he was from [[Fihr|فِهْر]], from the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]].
And [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] came from his descendants. Now we said [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]], he had many sons. From those sons was [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]],
and he also had [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]], and he had other sons.
Okay, from his son [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]],
so we have [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]], and we have his son [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]]. Now [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]], he had a number of sons as well.
[[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]] had [[Hashim|هَاشِم]] and he had [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]], and he had other sons as well.
Now the son of [[Hashim|هَاشِم]]
was a boy named [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]].
So let's look at the generations here.
We have [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]], and we have his son [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]], and then we have his son [[Hashim|هَاشِم]], and then we have his son [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]].
So [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]] grew up
with his mother, because [[Hashim|هَاشِم]] died while [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]] was still a young boy.
And the mother of [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]] lived outside of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] actually. The mother of [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]], she was from, her family was from
outside of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]. So she kept her son with her outside of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
And the father of this boy, [[Hashim|هَاشِم]], had already died.
Now, when this boy grew up, when [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]] grew up, when he became adolescent, when he reached maturity,

his uncle, [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]], and [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]] was another one of the sons of [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]], and [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]] was the brother of [[Hashim|هَاشِم]].

So [[Hashim|هَاشِم]] passed away, and [[Hashim|هَاشِم]]'s son [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]] is growing up with his mother outside of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]. [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]] is still there in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
Now when [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]] becomes mature, when he becomes an adolescent, his uncle [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]] comes from [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to take the boy back to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
So he comes to the mother's house and says, 'I want to take my nephew, [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]], back to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] with me.'
And she said, 'No, how can you take my son away from me?'
And then [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]] said that, 'Your son, the son of my brother [[Hashim|هَاشِم]], he is a leader, and he cannot stay outside of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
He is from the leading family, and he needs to go back to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] now that he has reached age.'
So the mother said, 'Okay, let's leave it in his choice. Let him do whatever he wants to do. Let the boy decide for himself.
If he wants to stay with me, he can stay with me. If he wants to go with you, he can go with you.' So they gave the choice to [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]].

And [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]] said, 'I'm going to go back to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] with my uncle, [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]].' Because he wanted to be part of that honor of leading [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] and taking care of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
He didn't want to just stay outside with his mother.
So he goes with his uncle [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]], and they enter back into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
Now, it was known those days that slavery was very common, and the people would go outside of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] and they would buy slaves and they would come back into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].

So when [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]] came back with his nephew into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]—and his nephew's name was [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]]—when [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]] came back with his nephew [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]] back into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]],
the people see [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]] with this young boy, they don't know who he is, they think, 'Oh, [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]] has gone outside of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to buy a slave,
and he's bringing his slave back into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].'

So they call this young boy, they say he is [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]]. He is [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], the slave of [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]], even though that was not his name.
His name was [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]], but he became known as [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] because of that.
And [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], as you know, he is the grandfather of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.
Now [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], he had many sons. He had ten sons and he had six daughters. So he had sixteen children: ten sons and six daughters.
And amongst his sons was the father of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]].

This is the lineage of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ: [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Hashim|هَاشِم]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]].

This is the lineage of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ: [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Hashim|هَاشِم]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]].
So [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]], next week we will talk about [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] and we will talk about how he rediscovered the well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]].

The well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]] was buried for centuries, and how, what is the story of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] rediscovering that well. We will talk about that next week, [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]].

segments.translit: Wallahu a'lam, wa sallallahu wa sallama wa baraka 'ala nabiyyina Muhammadin wa 'ala alihi wa sahbihi ajma'in.

review.q: Which leader was responsible for bringing idol worship back to the Arabs?
review.a: [[Amr ibn Luhayy|عمرو بن لحي]] of the [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]] tribe is noted for introducing idols to the people after they had followed the way of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]].

review.q: Why did the tribe of [[Jurhum|جرهم]] bury the well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]] before leaving [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]?
review.a: They buried the well to prevent the tribe of [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], who had forcibly ousted them, from benefiting from its water.

review.q: Who mediated the conflict between [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] and [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], and what was the outcome?
review.a: [[Ya'mur ibn 'Awf|يَعْمُر بن عَوْف]] mediated the dispute and ruled in favor of [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]], returning the leadership of the city to the descendants of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]].

review.q: What was the purpose of the [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]] established by [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]]?
review.a: It served as a council hall for tribal meetings, war declarations, and social events like weddings or coming-of-age ceremonies.

review.q: How were the honors of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] divided between the sons of [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]] to settle their dispute?
review.a: The descendants of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]] kept the [[Kiswah|كسوة]] (covering), while the descendants of [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]] took responsibility for the Siqayah (provision of water).

review.q: Why did the family of [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]] have to import water from outside [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] for the [[hujjaj|حجاج]]?
review.a: The well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]] was still buried and hidden at that time, so they brought water from elsewhere and often mixed it with [[laban|لَبَن]] or honey for the pilgrims.

review.q: What lesson does the speaker draw from the sale of [[Dar al-Nadwah|دَار الندوة]] by a member of the line of [[Abd al-Dar|عَبْد الدَّار]]?
review.a: The event warns against the dangers of alcohol, as the hall was lost for a single bottle of wine, and shows that true honor lies in [[taqwa|تَقْوَى]] rather than material legacy.

review.q: How did the Prophet's grandfather, originally named [[Shaybah|شَيْبَة]], come to be called [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]]?
review.a: When his uncle [[al-Muttalib|الْمُطَّلِب]] brought him into the city, the people of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] mistook the boy for his uncle's slave, and the name stayed with him.
